caption:
This morning: OpenCode 2.0 made the case that code agents matter less on their own than the workflow built around them.

Unconfirmed at check time: Cursor’s benchmark paper appears to list Claude Code at 65.4% on Terminal-Bench.
$10: OpenCode now has hosted Go pricing, not just BYOK.
$60 vs $100: OpenCode can be cheaper than Cursor Pro+ and Claude Max if token burn stays under control.

The takeaway for teams is simple: measure the workflow, not just the demo. Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning post said OpenCode 2.0 pushes the idea that the agent is not the whole gain; the workflow around it has to change too. I went back in to check the numbers that sit around that claim.
First, Cursor’s paper lists Claude Code at 65.4% on Terminal-Bench, but we could not confirm that on the cited page.
Second, OpenCode is not only BYOK anymore. Its own docs now show hosted tiers at $10 and $40 a month.
Third, the pricing choice is really workflow choice. If your token burn stays low, OpenCode can undercut Cursor at $60 and Claude at $100.
My take: workflow matters more than demos if costs stay visible. If you use it, what do you see? Comment CHECK and tell me.
